title: Finite type of an Artinian local algebra is detected on its residue field
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with $A$ Artinian local: it has a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and every descending chain of ideals stabilizes. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-field]. Then $A$ is finitely generated as an $R$-algebra if and only if $k$ is finitely generated as an $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is of finite type if and only if $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 02HV (lemma-artinian-finite-type); algebraic form is algebra.tex Tag 07DT (lemma-essentially-of-finite-type-into-artinian-local), part (2).

proof.text: If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $A$ as an $R$-algebra, their images generate $k$: lift any element of $k$ to $A$ and reduce its polynomial expression modulo $\mathfrak m$. This proves the forward implication directly from [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

Conversely choose algebra generators $\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_n$ of $k$ over $R$ and lifts $a_i\in A$. Let $C\subseteq A$ be the image of $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A$, $x_i\mapsto a_i$. The composite $C\to k$ is surjective, so $k$ is generated by $1$ as a $C$-module. The Jacobson radical $J(A)$ is the intersection of the maximal ideals, hence is $\mathfrak m$ because $A$ is local. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-finite-over-residue-finite] to $C\hookrightarrow A$: $A$ is Artinian and $A/J(A)=k$ is a finite $C$-module. Thus $A$ has finitely many $C$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$.

source.place: Tag 07DT (lemma-essentially-of-finite-type-into-artinian-local), part (2), converse via part (1); replace its polynomial source by its image

proof.text: Every $a\in A$ has the form $\sum_j c_jb_j$ with $c_j\in C$, and each $c_j$ is a polynomial in $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ with coefficients from $R$. Consequently $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_t$ generate $A$ as an $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], proving the converse.

source.place: Tag 07DT (lemma-essentially-of-finite-type-into-artinian-local), part (2), last sentence: finite over a finite-type algebra

proof.text: For $B=A$ or $B=k$, consider $g_B:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the map on whole affine charts is the given $R\to B$. If $g_B$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] applied to these charts makes $B$ finite type over $R$. Conversely, if $B$ is finite type over $R$, use these same whole charts at every point in [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] to obtain that $g_B$ is locally of finite type.

source.place: Tags 01T1 (definition-finite-type) and 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), applied to whole affine charts

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime], $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has one point; $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every inverse image of an affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is therefore empty or a singleton. Every open cover of such a set has a finite subcover (zero opens for the empty set, one containing the point otherwise), so both $g_A$ and $g_k$ are quasi-compact. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], each is of finite type exactly when it is locally of finite type. Step 4 translates the algebraic equivalence of steps 1–3 into the asserted scheme equivalence.

source.place: Tag 02HV (lemma-artinian-finite-type), singleton spectrum argument; Tag 01T1, finite type = locally finite type and quasi-compact
